p.src: Now Lu Su, acting on Zhou Yu’s instructions, went straight to Zhuge Liang’s boat to sound him out. Zhuge Liang welcomed him aboard, and they sat facing each other in the small craft. Lu Su said, “I have been occupied with military preparations these past few days and have missed the opportunity to seek your counsel.” Zhuge Liang said, “For my part, I have yet to congratulate the Commander-in-Chief.” Lu Su asked, “Congratulate him on what?” Zhuge Liang replied, “Gongjin sent you to discover whether I knew of the matter or not. That very matter is cause for congratulation.” Lu Su turned pale with fright and asked, “How did you come to know of it, Master?” Zhuge Liang said, “That stratagem was only good enough to deceive Jiang Gan. Though Cao Cao was fooled for a time, he must already have realized the truth; he is simply unwilling to admit his mistake. Now that Cai Mao and Zhang Yun are dead, Jiangdong has nothing to fear. How could this not merit congratulations? I hear Cao Cao has appointed Mao Jie and Yu Jin to replace them as commanders of the navy. In the hands of those two, his fleet is doomed, one way or another.”

p.src: Hearing this, Lu Su was left speechless. After stammering evasively for some time, he took leave of Zhuge Liang and returned. Zhuge Liang cautioned him, “I trust you will not tell Gongjin that I knew of this beforehand. I fear his jealousy will be aroused and he will again seek some pretext to harm me.” Lu Su promised and departed. But when he returned to Zhou Yu, he had no choice but to relate everything that had happened. Zhou Yu cried in alarm, “This man must by no means be allowed to live! I am resolved to behead him!” Lu Su remonstrated, “If you kill Zhuge Liang, Cao Cao will only laugh at us.” Zhou Yu said, “I shall have just grounds for beheading him, so that he dies with no cause for complaint.” Lu Su asked, “On what just grounds will you behead him?” Zhou Yu replied, “Ask no more, Zijing. You will see tomorrow.”

p.src: The next day, Zhou Yu assembled his generals beneath his command tent and ordered Zhuge Liang summoned to discuss military affairs. Zhuge Liang came cheerfully. Once they were seated, Zhou Yu asked him, “We will soon engage Cao Cao’s army. In warfare on the water, which weapon should take precedence?” Zhuge Liang replied, “On the Great River, bows and arrows come first.” Zhou Yu said, “Your words accord perfectly with my own view. But our army is presently short of arrows. May I trouble you, Master, to oversee the making of one hundred thousand arrows for use against the enemy? This is official business; I trust you will not decline.” Zhuge Liang replied, “Since the Commander-in-Chief has entrusted me with the task, I shall naturally do my utmost. May I ask when the hundred thousand arrows will be required?” Zhou Yu said, “Can they be completed within ten days?” Zhuge Liang replied, “Cao Cao’s army is due to arrive at any moment. If we wait ten days, we shall certainly imperil our great undertaking.” Zhou Yu asked, “How many days do you reckon you will need?” Zhuge Liang said, “Only three days are needed, and I shall duly deliver one hundred thousand arrows.” Zhou Yu said, “There is no jesting in the army.” Zhuge Liang replied, “How would I dare jest with the Commander-in-Chief! I am willing to sign a military pledge: if I fail to complete them in three days, I shall willingly suffer severe punishment.”

p.src: Zhou Yu was delighted. He summoned the military registrar to take Zhuge Liang’s written pledge in their presence, then entertained him with wine, saying, “When the military campaign is over, you shall be duly rewarded.” Zhuge Liang said, “It is already too late to begin today. The work will commence tomorrow. On the third day, you may send five hundred soldiers to the riverbank to carry away the arrows.” After drinking several cups, he took his leave. Lu Su asked, “Could this man be trying to deceive us?” Zhou Yu replied, “He has delivered himself to death; I did not force him. Now that he has openly given us a written pledge before everyone, even if wings sprouted from his sides, he could not fly away. I need only instruct the military craftsmen to delay deliberately and withhold the full supply of every material he requires. That way, he will certainly miss the deadline. When he is condemned then, what defence could he offer? You should go now and ascertain what he truly intends, then return and report to me.”

p.src: Lu Su obeyed and went to see Zhuge Liang. Zhuge Liang said, “I warned you, Zijing, not to tell Gongjin, for he was bound to try to harm me. I never thought you would refuse to conceal it for me. And sure enough, today he has stirred up fresh trouble. How can a hundred thousand arrows possibly be made in three days? You alone can save me, Zijing!” Lu Su replied, “You brought this calamity upon yourself. How can I possibly save you?” Zhuge Liang said, “I ask you to lend me twenty boats, each manned by thirty soldiers. Have every boat screened with blue cloth and more than a thousand bundles of straw arranged along its two sides. I have a wondrous use for them. I guarantee that on the third day there will be one hundred thousand arrows. But you must not let Gongjin learn of this as well. If he knows, my plan will fail.” Lu Su agreed, though he did not understand Zhuge Liang’s intent. When he returned to report to Zhou Yu, he indeed made no mention of the borrowed boats; he merely said that Zhuge Liang required none of the usual materials—arrow bamboo, feathers, glue, or lacquer—and had some method of his own. Deeply suspicious, Zhou Yu said, “We shall see how he answers me after three days!”

p.src: Now Lu Su privately assigned twenty swift, light boats, each with more than thirty men aboard, and had the cloth screens, bundles of straw, and all other necessities fully prepared to await Zhuge Liang’s orders. On the first day there was no sign of activity from Zhuge Liang, and on the second day he still made no move. In the fourth watch of the third night, Zhuge Liang secretly invited Lu Su aboard one of the boats. Lu Su asked, “Why have you summoned me?” Zhuge Liang replied, “I have specially invited you to come with me to collect the arrows.” Lu Su asked, “Where are we going to collect them?” Zhuge Liang said, “Ask no questions, Zijing. You will see when we arrive.” He then ordered the twenty boats linked together with long ropes, and they set out directly toward the northern bank. That night a great fog blanketed the sky. Over the Yangtze it was denser still, so that nothing could be seen even at arm’s length. Zhuge Liang urged the boats onward, and truly the fog was immense! p.src: By the fifth watch that night, the boats had drawn near Cao Cao’s naval stockade. Zhuge Liang ordered the boats arranged in a line, bows to the west and sterns to the east, and had the men beat their drums and raise battle cries. Lu Su cried in alarm, “What shall we do if Cao Cao’s troops all come out against us?” Zhuge Liang laughed. “I am certain Cao Cao will not dare come out in such dense fog. Let us simply drink and make merry. When the fog lifts, we shall return.”

p.src: Meanwhile, in Cao Cao’s camp, Mao Jie and Yu Jin heard the drums and battle cries and hurried to report the alarm to Cao Cao. Cao Cao issued an order: “A dense fog obscures the river. Since the enemy has come upon us without warning, there must be an ambush. On no account are you to move rashly. Deploy the naval archers and crossbowmen and have them shoot indiscriminately.” He also sent men to the land camp to summon Zhang Liao and Xu Huang, ordering each to bring three thousand archers and crossbowmen to the riverbank at once and reinforce the shooting. By the time this order arrived, Mao Jie and Yu Jin, fearing that the southern forces might break into the naval stockade, had already posted archers and crossbowmen before it and begun shooting.

p.src: Before long, the archers and crossbowmen from the land camp also arrived. More than ten thousand men in all shot into the river, their arrows falling like rain. Zhuge Liang ordered the boats turned around, their bows now east and sterns west, and had them press close to the naval stockade to receive the arrows while the men continued beating drums and shouting. When the sun rose high and the fog dispersed, Zhuge Liang ordered the boats withdrawn and they sped back. The bundles of straw along both sides of all twenty boats were thickly covered with arrows. Zhuge Liang ordered the soldiers on every boat to cry out in unison, “Many thanks to the Prime Minister for the arrows!” By the time word reached Cao Cao inside his camp, the boats, light and aided by the swift current, had already gone more than twenty li. Pursuit was impossible, and Cao Cao’s regret knew no bounds.

p.src: Kongming returned to their boat and said to Lu Su, “Each boat now carries some five or six thousand arrows. Without expending the least effort of Jiangdong, we have obtained more than a hundred thousand arrows. Would it not be most convenient to use them against Cao Cao’s army tomorrow?” Lu Su said, “Master, you are truly superhuman! How did you know there would be such a heavy fog today?” Kongming replied, “A commander who understands neither the heavens nor the terrain, knows neither the Qimen arts nor the principles of yin and yang, studies no battle formations, and comprehends no military situation is a mere mediocrity. Three days ago, I had already calculated that a heavy fog would descend today; hence I dared accept the three-day deadline. Gongjin ordered me to finish in ten days, though neither craftsmen nor materials were readily available; by fastening this elegant little charge upon me, he plainly meant to kill me. But my life rests with Heaven—how could Gongjin harm me?” Lu Su bowed in complete admiration.

Kongming had them taken from the boats, and the total exceeded a hundred thousand. All were carried into the central command tent and delivered. Lu Su went in to see Zhou Yu and recounted in full how Kongming had obtained the arrows. p.src: Shortly afterward, Kongming entered the camp to see Zhou Yu. Zhou Yu came out of his tent to welcome him and said admiringly, “Your marvelous foresight commands the deepest respect.” Kongming replied, “It was merely a trifling stratagem. What is there to marvel at?” Zhou Yu invited Kongming into the tent to drink with him. Zhou Yu said, “Yesterday my lord sent an envoy urging me to advance, but I have yet to devise an extraordinary plan. I beg you to instruct me.” Kongming said, “I am but a commonplace mediocrity. How could I possess any marvelous plan?” Zhou Yu said, “Yesterday I inspected Cao Cao’s naval stockade. It was exceptionally orderly and disciplined, and cannot be attacked lightly. I have conceived a plan, though I do not know whether it will serve. I would be grateful if you would judge it for me.” Kongming said, “Commander, say nothing yet. Let each of us write upon his palm, and then see whether our thoughts agree.”

p.src: Zhou Yu was delighted. He ordered brush and inkstone brought, secretly wrote first, and then passed them to Kongming. Kongming likewise wrote in secret. The two drew their seats together, revealed the characters in their palms, looked at one another’s writing, and both burst out laughing. It turned out that the character in Zhou Yu’s palm was “fire,” and in Kongming’s palm was likewise “fire.” Zhou Yu said, “Since the two of us see the matter alike, no doubt remains. I trust you will not divulge it.” Kongming replied, “This is the common business of our two houses. How could it be divulged? I reckon that although Cao Cao has twice suffered from this stratagem of mine, he still will not take precautions against it. Commander, you may now carry it out to the full.” When they had finished drinking, they parted; none of the generals knew what had passed.

p.src: Meanwhile, Cao Cao was deeply vexed at having lost a full hundred and fifty or sixty thousand arrows for nothing. Xun You offered a plan: “With Zhou Yu and Zhuge Liang devising stratagems in Jiangdong, it will be difficult to defeat them quickly. We should send men to Eastern Wu to feign surrender, serve as spies within, and relay intelligence. Only then can we make our designs against it.” Cao Cao said, “Your words accord exactly with my own thought. Who in our army do you think could execute this plan?” Xun You replied, “Cai Mao has been executed, but members of the Cai clan are all still in the army. His clansmen Cai Zhong and Cai He are now serving as deputy generals. Prime Minister, you may bind them to you with favors and send them to feign surrender. Eastern Wu will surely suspect nothing.” Cao Cao followed his counsel. That night he secretly summoned the two men to his tent and instructed them: “Take a small number of soldiers with you and go to Eastern Wu to feign surrender. Whenever there is any development, send someone to report it secretly. Once the deed is accomplished, you shall receive high rank and rich rewards. Harbor no disloyal thought!” The two replied, “Our wives and children are all in Jingzhou. How would we dare harbor disloyal thoughts? Prime Minister, have no doubts. We two will surely take the heads of Zhou Yu and Zhuge Liang and present them before your command.” Cao Cao rewarded them generously. The next day, the two took five hundred soldiers, boarded several boats, and sailed with the wind toward the southern bank.

p.src: Now Zhou Yu was attending to plans for advancing the army when a sudden report came that boats from north of the river had reached its mouth. Their occupants claimed to be Cai Mao’s kinsmen Cai He and Cai Zhong and had come expressly to surrender. Zhou Yu summoned them in. The two men wept, bowed, and said, “Our elder brother was innocent, yet the villain Cao had him killed. We wish to avenge our brother and have come expressly to surrender. We beg you to accept us and allow us to serve in the vanguard.” Zhou Yu was delighted and rewarded them handsomely, then at once ordered them to lead the vanguard with Gan Ning. The two bowed their thanks, believing their ruse had succeeded. Zhou Yu secretly summoned Gan Ning and instructed him: “These two have come without their families. Their surrender is false; Cao Cao sent them as spies. I now mean to turn their scheme against them and have them transmit intelligence. Treat them cordially, but remain secretly on guard. On the day we send forth the army, they must first be killed as sacrifices to the banners. You must be exceedingly careful and make no mistake.”

p.src: Gan Ning accepted the command and departed. Lu Su went in to see Zhou Yu and said, “Cai Zhong and Cai He’s surrender is most probably false. You must not take them into service.” Zhou Yu rebuked him: “They have come to surrender because Cao Cao killed their elder brother and they wish to avenge him. What deceit is there in that? If you are so suspicious, how can you ever welcome the worthy men of the realm?” Lu Su withdrew in silence and went to tell Kongming, who merely smiled and said nothing. Lu Su asked, “Why do you smile, Kongming?” Kongming replied, “I am laughing because you, Zijing, do not understand Gongjin’s stratagem. With the Great River lying broad between the armies, it is exceedingly difficult for spies to come and go. Cao Cao has sent Cai Zhong and Cai He to feign surrender and secretly spy upon our army. Gongjin is turning the scheme against him and intends precisely to have them carry reports. In war, deception is never rejected. Gongjin’s plan is correct.” Only then did Lu Su understand.

p.src: Now Zhou Yu was sitting in his tent at night when he suddenly saw Huang Gai steal into the camp to meet him. Zhou Yu asked, “Gongfu, since you have come by night, you must surely have some excellent counsel for me.” Huang Gai replied, “The enemy is numerous and we are few. We should not remain at a standoff for long. Why not attack them with fire?” Zhou Yu asked, “Who taught you to propose this plan?” Huang Gai replied, “It arose from my own thought; no one else taught it to me.” Zhou Yu said, “I intend exactly the same. That is why I have retained the false defectors Cai Zhong and Cai He, so that intelligence may pass through them. My sole regret is that I have no one to carry out a false surrender on my behalf.” Huang Gai said, “I am willing to carry out the plan.” Zhou Yu said, “Unless you suffer some hardship, how can they be persuaded to believe you?” Huang Gai replied, “I have received profound favor from the Sun family. Even if my liver and brains were smeared upon the earth, I would neither resent nor regret it.” Zhou Yu bowed and thanked him, saying, “If you are willing to endure this self-injury stratagem, it will be the greatest fortune for Jiangdong.” Huang Gai said, “Even if I die, I shall bear no resentment.” He then took his leave and departed.

p.src: The next day, Zhou Yu beat the drum and assembled all the generals beneath his command tent. Kongming was also present. Zhou Yu said, “Cao Cao leads a million men, whose camps extend for more than three hundred li. He cannot be defeated in a single day. I now order each general to draw three months’ provisions and prepare to resist the enemy.” Before he had finished speaking, Huang Gai stepped forward and said, “Never mind three months; even if you issued thirty months’ provisions, it would be of no use! If we can defeat him this month, then defeat him; but if we cannot defeat him this month, we can only follow Zhang Zibu’s advice, cast aside our armor, reverse our weapons, face north, and surrender!” Zhou Yu’s expression changed abruptly, and he cried in fury, “I have received my lord’s command to direct the army and defeat Cao Cao. Whoever dares speak again of surrender shall be beheaded. Now, when the two armies stand opposed, you dare utter such words and undermine the spirit of my troops. Unless I take your head, I cannot command the obedience of the host!” He shouted to the attendants to take Huang Gai away, behead him, and report back. Huang Gai likewise cried angrily, “I have followed General Who Breaks the Caitiffs in campaigns across the southeast, serving three generations of the Sun house. Where were you then?”

p.src: Zhou Yu flew into a rage and ordered that he be beheaded at once. Gan Ning stepped forward and pleaded, “Gongfu is a veteran minister of Eastern Wu. I beg you to show him mercy.” Zhou Yu shouted, “How dare you say another word and disrupt my discipline!” He first berated his attendants and had Gan Ning driven out with a hail of blows. All the officers knelt and pleaded, “Huang Gai’s offense indeed deserves death, but executing him would harm the army. We beg the Commander-in-Chief to forgive him and record the offense for the time being. It will not be too late to behead him after Cao Cao has been defeated.” Zhou Yu’s anger did not abate, and the officers continued to plead desperately. Zhou Yu said, “Were it not out of regard for all of you, he would most certainly be beheaded! For now, I shall spare his life!” He ordered his attendants to throw Huang Gai down and administer one hundred strokes across his back as punishment for his offense. The officers again begged him to relent, but Zhou Yu overturned the command table, drove them back with angry shouts, and ordered the beating carried out. Huang Gai was stripped, dragged to the ground, and given fifty strokes across the back. When the officers once more pleaded desperately for mercy, Zhou Yu leapt to his feet, pointed at Huang Gai, and cried, “Do you dare make light of me? The remaining fifty strokes shall be recorded for now. If you show negligence again, you shall be punished for both offenses!” Still muttering angrily, he went into his tent.

p.src: The officers helped Huang Gai up. His flesh had been split open and blood gushed from his wounds. They carried him back to his own camp, where he lost consciousness several times. Everyone who came to inquire after him was moved to tears. Lu Su also visited him, then went to Kongming’s boat and said, “Today Gongjin angrily punished Gongfu. Since we are all his subordinates, we dared not brave his wrath and remonstrate too forcefully. But you, Master, are a guest. Why did you stand by with folded arms and say nothing?” Kongming laughed and said, “Zijing, you are trying to deceive me.” Lu Su replied, “Since I crossed the river with you, I have never deceived you in a single matter. Why do you say this now?” Kongming said, “Surely you know that Gongjin’s brutal beating of Huang Gongfu today was part of his scheme? Why, then, would you have me dissuade him?” Only then did Lu Su understand. Kongming said, “Without using the ruse of self-inflicted suffering, how could they deceive Cao Cao? They will now surely have Huang Gongfu pretend to surrender, while arranging for Cai Zhong and Cai He to report the matter. When you see Gongjin, you must not tell him that I knew of the scheme beforehand. Merely say that I too resent the Commander-in-Chief, and that will suffice.”

p.src: Lu Su took his leave and went to see Zhou Yu, who invited him into the inner part of the tent. Lu Su asked, “Why did you punish Huang Gongfu so severely today?” Zhou Yu asked, “Do the officers resent me?” Lu Su replied, “Many are troubled at heart.” Zhou Yu asked, “And what does Kongming think?” Lu Su replied, “He too resents the Commander-in-Chief for being excessively heartless.” Zhou Yu laughed and said, “This time I have managed to deceive even him.” Lu Su asked, “What do you mean?” Zhou Yu said, “The severe beating I gave Huang Gai today was part of a scheme. I intend to have him feign surrender. First we had to use the ruse of self-inflicted suffering to deceive Cao Cao; then, from within his forces, we shall attack with fire and gain victory.” Lu Su privately marveled at Kongming’s extraordinary insight but did not dare reveal it.

p.src: Meanwhile, Huang Gai lay in his tent, and all the officers came to inquire after him. Huang Gai said nothing and merely heaved long sighs. Suddenly it was announced that the staff officer Kan Ze had come to visit him. Huang Gai ordered that he be admitted to his bedside, then dismissed all attendants. Kan Ze asked, “Can it be that you bear some grudge against the Commander-in-Chief?” Huang Gai replied, “No.” Kan Ze asked, “Then was your punishment perhaps a ruse of self-inflicted suffering?” Huang Gai asked, “How did you know?” Kan Ze replied, “From observing Gongjin’s actions, I had already guessed eight or nine parts out of ten.” Huang Gai said, “I have received generous favor from three generations of the lords of Wu, yet have had no means to repay it. Therefore I proposed this scheme to defeat Cao Cao. Though I suffer, I bear no resentment. I have looked throughout the army and found no one whom I could trust with this secret. Only you have always possessed a loyal and righteous heart, so I venture to confide my secret to you.” Kan Ze said, “In telling me this, you can only mean that you wish me to deliver a false letter of surrender.” Huang Gai replied, “That is indeed my intention. I do not know whether you are willing.” Kan Ze gladly agreed to undertake the task. Just as the verse says:
